description.purpose: A display as ONE cell that owns a NAME: the colony's one listener hands it every connection whose first path segment is its mount, and behind that name it serves an HTTP + WebSocket surface over an object tree in its own cell.db, a component library that is data rather than code, and server-side rendering that is materialised -- a page load answers from memory and costs no cell call. It ships with the Vision token stylesheet, so a display looks like something before anybody has designed anything.
description.use_when: Wherever a colony needs a surface of its own: one instance per display, each with its own mount. Instantiate it with add_nodes and give the instance the name it should answer to via override_params -- the template's `web` is the first one, not the only one. The page is then at /<mount>/ on the colony's listener. Wire the event lane out of the cell if anything should listen to what a person does on the page; a display nobody listens to still works, its events just dead-letter visibly.
description.not_in_scope: No authentication and no TLS, ever (R-W8-2): put a reverse proxy in front of the colony's listener. No listener of its own -- since `web@2.0.0` there is no port and no bind, and a params document carrying either is refused with the migration named. No routing of its own beyond the mount -- the pages table is the only route source, and there is no cell.surface key any more: it was removed together with the /surface/* path it declared, so a tree that still carries one is refused at boot rather than served by nothing. No application logic: it renders what somebody sent it and reports what a person did; what that means is the topology's business. And no design opinion beyond the token sheet -- components are rows, and a model may define its own at runtime.
examples: DIRECTIONS - in: object.create / object.update / object.move / object.delete / component.define / page.set / query as tool_call turns; two or more in one body are answered as one bundle with a results[] slot, the store convention. out: a semantic browser event as a source emission on hop.route 'event' (header carries event_name, session_id, page_route, and user_id when identity_header is set), and a tool_result reply per op. A browser event on a prop the component declared editable never appears out here -- it is absorbed as local CRUD plus a diff to every viewer.

THE MOUNT IS THE IDENTITY - a second display is a second instance with its own mount, and the page lives at /<mount>/ on the colony's listener. Since `web@2.0.0` there is no port to own: port and bind are gone, and a document carrying either is refused with `port: removed in web 2.0.0 -- the cell is reached at /<mount>/ on the colony's listener; drop the key and name a mount`. Rename a display with {"params": {"mount": "screen"}}; the new name is registered on the cell's next life, so the running one keeps answering under the old one until then.

A PROXY MAY PUT IT ANYWHERE - the shell writes every link from X-Forwarded-Prefix plus the mount, so `location ^~ /egon/` with `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Prefix /egon` serves the page at https://host/egon/<mount>/ with its socket and its bundles alongside. A prefix outside ^/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]{0,200}$ is ignored rather than trusted. Name the proxy's identity header in identity_header and every semantic event of a socket carries hop.user_id.

WHAT SHIPS IN THE SEED - one page at '/', a stack root, a text child, and the Vision token stylesheet as an asset row at /vision.css. The seed loads once, on first spawn only, so a display that an operator has emptied stays empty across a wake.
